candidate_units.title: Standalone provider-neutral normalized result and provenance validator
candidate_units.scope: New worker/src/providerResultValidation.ts and worker/src/providerResultValidation.test.ts, a pure module with no I/O. It exports validateProviderResult(binding, output, nowIso). binding = {schemaVersion, provider, taskId, laneId, permitId, envelopeId, envelopeRevision, envelopeFingerprint, scopeFingerprint, cadSha256, drawingSha256|null, quantity, allowedHosts, authorizedAt, expiresAt}; output = VendorQuoteAdapterOutput from worker/src/types.ts. It returns {kind:'validated_offer_set', offers} or one finite sanitized failure {kind:'failure', code, retryable}. Reuse evaluateProviderAdapterContract (worker/src/adapters/providerAdapterContract.ts:247) for offer-level checks; do not fork its rules. Add checks for: exact binding match, a freshness window, rejecting native-currency and synthetic or simulated payloads (rawPayload.fixtureKind), rejecting adapter-asserted admission or permit claims, HTTPS-only quoteUrl, and constrained geographicOrigin with a provider_text source. Xometry one-to-many variants must pass intact using fixtures from worker/src/adapters/xometryOffers.test.ts. No wiring into index.ts and no persistence.
candidate_units.acceptance: The new test file passes with a table of at least 14 cases, each asserting a distinct failure code: provider, task, lane, permit, envelope, scope and package mismatch; quantity mismatch; non-finite or non-positive price; EUR native evidence; duplicate providerOptionId; non-HTTPS or off-allowlist quoteUrl; collection time before authorizedAt or after expiresAt; domestic origin without a provider_text source; synthetic fixtureKind; unknown schemaVersion; admission claim inside rawPayload. One case asserts that a Xometry multi-variant output validates with every variant preserved in order. A static assertion shows the module imports no playwright, supabase or fetch. `npm --prefix worker run verify` and `npm run lint` pass, and existing xometryOffers and providerAdapterContract tests are unchanged and passing.
candidate_units.verification_plan: Failure-first: commit the test file first, then run `npx vitest run worker/src/providerResultValidation.test.ts` and confirm it fails (module missing). Implement and rerun until it passes. Then `npx vitest run worker/src/adapters/xometryOffers.test.ts worker/src/adapters/providerAdapterContract.test.ts worker/src/adapters/nativeCurrencyEvaluation.test.ts`, `npm --prefix worker run verify`, `npm run lint`, and finally `npm run verify`.
candidate_units.risks: Linear still lists OVD-380, OVD-413 and OVD-414 as blockers, and the Oct 3 ordering puts 461–464 after 567/568 (see open question). The binding type should later be mapped from #568's ProviderDispatchEnvelope; keep it local now to stay off the unmerged stack. Failure codes must line up with OVD-377 diagnostics. There is a risk of duplicating providerAdapterContract rules if it is not reused.

open_questions.question: Acceptance-criteria conflict: the seven-provider portfolio versus 'at least five same-package 6061-T6 CNC automatic sources'. Which governs 1.0 enablement, and how is a CNC shortfall handled?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The text pulls two ways. ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md:19-22 says 'The named 1.0 portfolio is Xometry, Fictiv, Quickparts, Weerg, Geomiq, RMFG, and OSH Cut. RMFG and OSH Cut qualify only through separately qualified process-specific envelopes'. ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md:94-98 says OVD-319 may enable only 'an explicitly named CNC-eligible set containing Xometry plus at least four additional qualifying providers from the named 1.0 portfolio'. ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md:199-204 requires 'Xometry and at least four additional automatic quote providers from the named 1.0 portfolio ... production-certified for the same CNC validation envelope'. ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md:234-237 requires 'one current ... live offer from each of at least five CNC-qualified providers in the named 1.0 portfolio for the same disclosed package'. Also PLAN.md:454-457 ('Keep the CNC-first same-package proof for at least five CNC-qualified sources ... do not require seven CNC offers'), PLAN.md:206-207 ('A substitution cannot silently remove a named provider'), PRD.md:64-68 and TEST_STRATEGY.md:312-316 ('rejects fewer than five qualifying providers'). Only five of the named seven are CNC, so all five must pass with no slack. Weerg (manifest:35) and Geomiq (manifest:28) evidence only aluminum_6082 and evaluate 6061 as material_unknown, and Xometry's manifest capabilities are all unknown. OVD-385 (Sep 26) still says 'five admitted providers'. As written, the CNC gate may be unmeetable.
open_questions.options: (a) Keep ≥5 CNC and require 6061-T6 evidence from Weerg and Geomiq (or change the validation material). (b) Lower the CNC same-package count and qualify RMFG and OSH Cut separately. (c) Allow substitutes from outside the named seven that have 6061 evidence (RapidDirect, Protolabs, SendCutSend), which PLAN.md:199-207 currently excludes. (d) Accept 6082 as comparable for the validation package.
